headline: Japan plans CO2 storage off Malaysia; 10 years or more after closure, the Government takes over
context: Malaysia's 2025 CCUS Act lets permit holders import CO2 captured abroad for permanent storage. Malaysia and Japan signed a CCS cooperation memo in October 2025; talks on a shipping deal were still running in September.

cards.big: Japan picked three projects in 2024 to store about 10 million tonnes of CO2 a year off Malaysia. The deal to ship it there was still being finalised in September.
cards.sub: Two sites fall under the 2025 federal CCUS Act; Sarawak applies its own rules to the third. Each says who watches a site after it closes.
trace: JOGMEC selection 28 Jun 2024 and project appendix: three Malaysian projects, ~3 + 1.9-2.9 + ~5 Mtpa = 9.9-10.9 Mtpa planned (Stage 3 VERIFIED; brief S7)

Memorandum of Co-Operation, Malaysia-METI, CCS, signed 17 Oct 2025 (Stage 3 omitted fact; Ministry of Economy AZEC statement, brief S9e); bilateral arrangements 'towards the finalisation', 15 Sep 2026 (Stage 3; brief S9a)

Act 870 s. 2 Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S1a); Sarawak Cap. 85 s. 3(3) read with Land (Carbon Storage) Rules 2022 (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S8a, S8b); P.U.(A) 346/2025 regs 41-45 and Sarawak rules 41-43 (INTRODUCED, opened 18 Nov 2026)

cards.big: On 23 Oct 2026 Petronas, TotalEnergies and Mitsui signed a joint venture agreement for a CO2 storage hub off Peninsular Malaysia's east coast, up to 5 Mt a year.
cards.sub: It matches one of Japan's 2024 projects but will also take Malaysian and regional CO2. First injection is targeted as early as 2031.
trace: Petronas release 23 Oct 2026 and Bernama same day: JVA, PCCSV, TotalEnergies EP CCS Malaysia, Mitsui; 'up to 5 million tonnes per annum' phase 1; 'as early as 2031'; FID ahead; hub 'to receive CO2 domestically and regionally, including potential cross-border CO2 shipments' (Stage 3 VERIFIED; brief S12d)
Corresponds to the Southern Offshore Peninsular Malaysia project on JOGMEC's 2024 list (Stage 3 VERIFIED, preferred wording)

cards.big: Federal rules hand a closed site's monitoring and repair to the Government at least 10 years after closure, once its CO2 is shown to be contained.
cards.sub: Until then the operator holds financial security. After, a fund of Government money and operator levies pays; the operator stays liable for its fault.
trace: P.U.(A) 346/2025 reg 42: transfer 'upon request' if (b) proof that CO2 'will be completely and permanently contained', (c) 'a minimum period of at least ten years has lapsed since the issuance of a storage site closure certificate', (d) levies paid, (e) sealed and decommissioned, (f) seabed made good; reg 44 extension (Stage 3 VERIFIED; INTRODUCED wording re-checked against the gazette text, S1c)

P.U.(A) 346/2025 regs 14, 32(1)(b)-(c): financial security 'valid and has effect before commencement of injection' and 'remains effective until the transfer of obligations' (Stage 3 omitted fact; INTRODUCED, opened 18 Nov 2026, S1c)

Act 870 ss. 41(2), 42(1): Fund of Government sums, injection levy and investment income pays Government's post-transfer stewardship costs; s. 32(3) fault, negligence, deceit, due diligence (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S1a)

cards.big: Sarawak's 2022 rules set at least 20 years before handover, shorter only if containment is proven, and charge a contribution sized to cover the state's costs after it.
cards.sub: Federal law funds its side through an injection levy that may not be raised because of fund withdrawals. We found no gazetted rate.
trace: Sarawak Land (Carbon Storage) Rules 2022, Swk. L.N. 349/2022: r. 41(4) 'The minimum period shall not be less than twenty years from the date of the closure of the storage site or to a reduced minimum period if the Authority is satisfied that transfer conditions ... are fulfilled'; r. 41(5)(a) containment; r. 42(1) 'financial contribution ... sufficient to cover the estimated post-transfer costs'; r. 43(5) recovery for fault (Stage 3 omitted fact; INTRODUCED, gazette text opened 18 Nov 2026, S8b)

Act 870 s. 30(2)(b) 'shall not be increased due to withdrawals from the Fund or risks associated with other offshore storage projects' (Stage 3 VERIFIED; wording narrowed per Stage 3 OVERCLAIM flag); no levy order identified in AGC records reviewed 18 Nov 2026; P.U.(A) 346/2025 sets no rate (Stage 3 UNVERIFIED-bounded; card says 'We found'; S2, S1c)

cards.big: The asymmetry is built in. The capturing country reports the climate gain; after handover, the country that buries the CO2 inherits the duty to watch it.
trace: 2006 IPCC Guidelines Vol 2 Ch 5 s. 5.10 p. 5.20: Country A reports CO2 captured and exported; Country B reports emissions from injection and storage sites; Ch 2 Eq 2.7 capture subtracted at source (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S3a, S3b)
Act 870 s. 32 and P.U.(A) 346/2025 reg 42: monitoring passes to the Government after transfer (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S1a, S1c)

cards.big: Think of a landlord who takes back a sealed storeroom only after the tenant has kept it ten years, proved it tight and paid in. From then on, the upkeep is the landlord's.
trace: P.U.(A) 346/2025 reg 42(b)-(d): ten years, containment proven, levies paid (S1c); Act 870 s. 42(1) Government bears post-transfer stewardship costs (S1a)

cards.big: Malaysia has written who watches a closed reservoir, and when. Before the first import permit, publish the levy rate and the Japan terms so Malaysians see who pays.
trace: Act 870 ss. 19-20 import permits; s. 30 levy by gazetted order; no levy order identified (S1a, S2); bilateral arrangement being finalised 15 Sep 2026 (S9a)

synthesis_notes: Over-integration calls. (1) Stage 2 asked to frame the post-closure fund as industry-funded and to add economic benefits; Stage 3 asked to describe potential residual public exposure. Both are right on different points and neither is averaged: the cards state what the law says (Government money, operator levies, operator financial security until transfer, operator fault liability kept) and drop the 'public bill' claim. No revenue figure is added: the only revenue figures found are Ministry of Economy/Petronas promotional estimates (brief CONTRADICTION 9 and Economic row), which fail the primary-source bar; the Economic lens is used for the joint-venture card instead. (2) Stage 2 flagged 'Sarawak regulates' as an overclaim on contested jurisdiction; Stage 3 verified that the Sarawak ordinance covers offshore CCS. The evidence supports stating what Sarawak's own rules provide and that Sarawak applies them (PETROS signed the M3 storage site agreement as Sarawak's CCUS resource manager); it does not support stating who wins any federal-state dispute, and Stage 3 found no primary showing that the Federal Court petitions concern carbon storage. Cards therefore describe each regime's own rules and take no side. (3) Stage 2 called 'fait accompli' loaded; the view drops it and names the decision point instead. Elevated word moves to 'asymmetry' in the reframe. Compression decisions. The '10 years or more' in the headline keeps 'at least'. Fact 2 keeps 'once the CO2 is shown to be contained' but drops the other four reg 42 conditions (levies paid, sealing, decommissioning, seabed made good) for length; the analogy carries 'paid in'. The IPCC 2005 retention estimate (very likely over 99% across 100 years for appropriately selected and managed sites) is not on a card; no card claims leakage is likely, and the reframe speaks of the duty to watch, not of leaks. Sarawak's rule 43(3) (licensee continues monitoring after permit termination 'until otherwise provided') is noted: the Sarawak card says only 'before handover', not that the state assumes monitoring on a fixed date.
